sanskrit: sa taṃ papraccha rājendro muniṃ maunavratānvitam na ca kiṃ cid uvācainaṃ sa muniḥ pṛcchato 'pi san
english: That king, best among kings, questioned the sage who was bound by a vow of silence; but the sage did not say anything to him, even though he was being asked.

sanskrit: tato rājā kṣucchramārtas taṃ muniṃ sthāṇuvat sthitam maunavratadharaṃ śāntaṃ sadyo manyuvaśaṃ yayau
english: Then the king, exhausted by hunger and fatigue, came immediately under the sway of anger toward that sage who stood like a post, observing his vow of silence, calm and quiet.

sanskrit: na bubodha hi taṃ rājā maunavratadharaṃ munim sa taṃ manyusamāviṣṭo dharṣayām āsa te pitā
english: Indeed the king did not understand that the sage was observing a vow of silence; possessed by anger, your father insulted him.

sanskrit: mṛtaṃ sarpaṃ dhanuṣkoṭyā samutkṣipya dharātalāt tasya śuddhātmanaḥ prādāt skandhe bharatasattama
english: Lifting a dead serpent from the ground with the tip of his bow, he placed it on the shoulder of that pure-souled one, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: na covāca sa medhāvī tam atho sādhv asādhu vā tasthau tathaiva cākrudhyan sarpaṃ skandhena dhārayan
english: But that wise sage said nothing to him — neither good nor ill — he remained just as he was, neither angry, carrying the serpent on his shoulder.

sanskrit: mantriṇa ūcuḥ tataḥ sa rājā rājendra skandhe tasya bhujaṃgamam muneḥ kṣutkṣāma āsajya svapuraṃ punar āyayau
english: The ministers said: Then that king, O best of kings, having placed the serpent on the shoulder of the sage — emaciated as he was from hunger — returned again to his own city.

sanskrit: ṛṣes tasya tu putro 'bhūd gavi jāto mahāyaśāḥ śṛṅgī nāma mahātejās tigmavīryo 'tikopanaḥ
english: But that sage had a son, born of a cow, of great fame, named Śṛṅgī, of great radiance, fierce in energy, and extremely wrathful.

sanskrit: brahmāṇaṃ so 'bhyupāgamya muniḥ pūjāṃ cakāra ha anujñāto gatas tatra śṛṅgī śuśrāva taṃ tadā sakhyuḥ sakāśāt pitaraṃ pitrā te dharṣitaṃ tathā
english: The sage had gone to pay homage to Brahman; having paid his respects and been given leave, Śṛṅgī went there, and at that point he heard from a friend that his father had been insulted by your father in that manner.

sanskrit: mṛtaṃ sarpaṃ samāsaktaṃ pitrā te janamejaya vahantaṃ kuruśārdūla skandhenānapakāriṇam
english: That his father was carrying on his shoulder a dead serpent placed there by your father, O Janamejaya, O tiger among the Kurus — the father who had done no wrong.

sanskrit: tapasvinam atīvātha taṃ munipravaraṃ nṛpa jitendriyaṃ viśuddhaṃ ca sthitaṃ karmaṇy athādbhute
english: A great ascetic, the foremost of sages, O king, one who had conquered the senses, pure, and engaged in wondrous action,

sanskrit: tapasā dyotitātmānaṃ sveṣv aṅgeṣu yataṃ tathā śubhācāraṃ śubhakathaṃ susthiraṃ tam alolupam
english: whose soul blazed with austerity, who was restrained in his own limbs, of auspicious conduct, of auspicious speech, perfectly steadfast and free from greed,

sanskrit: akṣudram anasūyaṃ ca vṛddhaṃ maunavrate sthitam śaraṇyaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ pitrā viprakṛtaṃ tava
english: not petty, without envy, aged, abiding in the vow of silence, a refuge for all beings — such a one had been wronged by your father.

sanskrit: śaśāpātha sa tac chrutvā pitaraṃ te ruṣānvitaḥ ṛṣeḥ putro mahātejā bālo 'pi sthavirair varaḥ
english: Having heard this, he cursed your father, filled with fury — the son of the sage, of great radiance, though a boy yet superior to elders.

sanskrit: sa kṣipram udakaṃ spṛṣṭvā roṣād idam uvāca ha pitaraṃ te 'bhisaṃdhāya tejasā prajvalann iva
english: Quickly touching water, he spoke these words in rage, blazing as it were with his fiery energy, directed against your father:

sanskrit: anāgasi gurau yo me mṛtaṃ sarpam avāsṛjat taṃ nāgas takṣakaḥ kruddhas tejasā sādayiṣyati saptarātrād itaḥ pāpaṃ paśya me tapaso balam
english: "He who placed a dead serpent on my innocent teacher — Takṣaka the serpent, in wrath, shall lay him low with his venom within seven nights from now. Wicked man, behold the power of my austerity!"

sanskrit: ity uktvā prayayau tatra pitā yatrāsya so 'bhavat dṛṣṭvā ca pitaraṃ tasmai śāpaṃ taṃ pratyavedayat
english: Having spoken thus, he went to where his father was; and having seen his father, he reported to him that curse.

sanskrit: sa cāpi muniśārdūlaḥ preṣayām āsa te pituḥ śapto 'si mama putreṇa yatto bhava mahīpate takṣakas tvāṃ mahārāja tejasā sādayiṣyati
english: And that tiger among sages also sent a messenger to your father: "You have been cursed by my son — be on your guard, O lord of the earth; Takṣaka, O great king, will lay you low with his venom."

sanskrit: śrutvā tu tad vaco ghoraṃ pitā te janamejaya yatto 'bhavat paritrastas takṣakāt pannagottamāt
english: Hearing those terrible words, your father, O Janamejaya, was on his guard, terrified of Takṣaka, the foremost of serpents.

sanskrit: tatas tasmiṃs tu divase saptame samupasthite rājñaḥ samīpaṃ brahmarṣiḥ kāśyapo gantum aicchata
english: Then when the seventh day arrived, the brahmarṣi Kāśyapa wished to go to the king's presence.

sanskrit: taṃ dadarśātha nāgendraḥ kāśyapaṃ takṣakas tadā tam abravīt pannagendraḥ kāśyapaṃ tvaritaṃ vrajan kva bhavāṃs tvarito yāti kiṃ ca kāryaṃ cikīrṣati
english: Then Takṣaka, lord of serpents, saw Kāśyapa and spoke to him as he was hurrying on his way: "Where does your honour go in such haste, and what deed does he intend to perform?"

sanskrit: kāśyapa uvāca yatra rājā kuruśreṣṭhaḥ parikṣin nāma vai dvija takṣakeṇa bhujaṃgena dhakṣyate kila tatra vai
english: Kāśyapa said: There where the king, best of the Kurus, known as Parīkṣit, is to be burned by the serpent Takṣaka — that is where I am going, O twice-born one.

sanskrit: gacchāmy ahaṃ taṃ tvaritaḥ sadyaḥ kartum apajvaram mayābhipannaṃ taṃ cāpi na sarpo dharṣayiṣyati
english: I go to him quickly to cure him at once of his affliction; one protected by me — the serpent shall not harm him.

sanskrit: takṣaka uvāca kimarthaṃ taṃ mayā daṣṭaṃ saṃjīvayitum icchasi brūhi kāmam ahaṃ te 'dya dadmi svaṃ veśma gamyatām
english: Takṣaka said: Why do you wish to revive the one bitten by me? Tell me your desire — I will grant it to you today; go to your own home.

sanskrit: mantriṇa ūcuḥ dhanalipsur ahaṃ tatra yāmīty uktaś ca tena saḥ tam uvāca mahātmānaṃ mānayañ ślakṣṇayā girā
english: The ministers said: He replied to him that he was going there out of desire for wealth; and Takṣaka, honouring that great-souled one, addressed him with conciliatory words:

sanskrit: yāvad dhanaṃ prārthayase tasmād rājñas tato 'dhikam gṛhāṇa matta eva tvaṃ saṃnivartasva cānagha
english: "Whatever wealth you desire from that king, take even more than that from me and turn back, O sinless one."

sanskrit: sa evam ukto nāgena kāśyapo dvipadāṃ varaḥ labdhvā vittaṃ nivavṛte takṣakād yāvad īpsitam
english: Thus addressed by the serpent, Kāśyapa, best among two-footed beings, having received from Takṣaka as much wealth as he desired, turned back.

sanskrit: tasmin pratigate vipre chadmanopetya takṣakaḥ taṃ nṛpaṃ nṛpatiśreṣṭha pitaraṃ dhārmikaṃ tava
english: After the brahmin departed, Takṣaka, approaching in disguise, that king — best of kings, your righteous father —

sanskrit: prāsādasthaṃ yattam api dagdhavān viṣavahninā tatas tvaṃ puruṣavyāghra vijayāyābhiṣecitaḥ
english: though he was on guard in his palace, burned him with the fire of his venom; then you, O tiger among men, were consecrated to victory.

sanskrit: etad dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ cāpi yathāvan nṛpasattama asmābhir nikhilaṃ sarvaṃ kathitaṃ te sudāruṇam
english: All this, seen and heard by us in full, O best of kings, we have related to you in its entirety — this most terrible thing.

sanskrit: śrutvā caitaṃ nṛpaśreṣṭha pārthivasya parābhavam asya carṣer uttaṅkasya vidhatsva yad anantaram
english: Having heard of this overthrow of the king, O best of rulers, and of this sage Uttaṅka as well, decide now what is to follow.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca etat tu śrotum icchāmi aṭavyāṃ nirjane vane saṃvādaṃ pannagendrasya kāśyapasya ca yat tadā
english: Janamejaya said: I wish to hear this — what was then the conversation between the lord of serpents and Kāśyapa in the lonely forest wilderness.

sanskrit: kena dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ cāpi bhavatāṃ śrotram āgatam śrutvā cātha vidhāsyāmi pannagāntakarīṃ matim
english: By whom was it seen and heard, and how did it reach your ears? Having heard it, I shall then resolve upon a course of action to destroy the serpents.

sanskrit: mantriṇa ūcuḥ śṛṇu rājan yathāsmākaṃ yenaitat kathitaṃ purā samāgamaṃ dvijendrasya pannagendrasya cādhvani
english: The ministers said: Listen, O king, as to how this was told to us before — the encounter on the road between the lord of twice-born ones and the lord of serpents.

sanskrit: tasmin vṛkṣe naraḥ kaś cid indhanārthāya pārthiva vicinvan pūrvam ārūḍhaḥ śuṣkaśākhaṃ vanaspatim abudhyamānau taṃ tatra vṛkṣasthaṃ pannagadvijau
english: On that tree, O lord of the earth, some man had previously climbed in search of firewood, to gather dry branches from the forest tree; the serpent and the twice-born one did not notice him sitting there in that tree.

sanskrit: sa tu tenaiva vṛkṣeṇa bhasmībhūto 'bhavat tadā dvijaprabhāvād rājendra jīvitaḥ savanaspatiḥ
english: He was reduced to ashes along with that very tree; but by the power of the twice-born one, O best of kings, he was restored to life together with the forest tree.

sanskrit: tena gatvā nṛpaśreṣṭha nagare 'smin niveditam yathāvṛttaṃ tu tat sarvaṃ takṣakasya dvijasya ca
english: He went and reported to this city, O best of kings, all that had happened — the entire account of Takṣaka and the twice-born one.

sanskrit: etat te kathitaṃ rājan yathāvṛttaṃ yathāśrutam śrutvā tu nṛpaśārdūla prakuruṣva yathepsitam
english: This has been told to you, O king, exactly as it occurred and as we heard it; having heard it, O tiger among kings, do now as you desire.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca mantriṇāṃ tu vacaḥ śrutvā sa rājā janamejayaḥ paryatapyata duḥkhārtaḥ pratyapiṃṣat kare karam
english: The Sūta said: Having heard the words of the ministers, king Janamejaya was tormented with grief; afflicted with sorrow, he wrung his hands.

sanskrit: niḥśvāsam uṣṇam asakṛd dīrghaṃ rājīvalocanaḥ mumocāśrūṇi ca tadā netrābhyāṃ pratataṃ nṛpaḥ uvāca ca mahīpālo duḥkhaśokasamanvitaḥ
english: Repeatedly he exhaled long hot sighs; the lotus-eyed king shed tears continuously from both eyes; and the lord of the earth, overwhelmed with grief and sorrow, spoke:

sanskrit: śrutvaitad bhavatāṃ vākyaṃ pitur me svargatiṃ prati niściteyaṃ mama matir yā vai tāṃ me nibodhata
english: "Having heard these words of yours regarding my father's passage to heaven, my resolve is firm — hear what it is from me.

sanskrit: anantaram ahaṃ manye takṣakāya durātmane pratikartavyam ity eva yena me hiṃsitaḥ pitā
english: I think that retribution must follow immediately against the wicked-souled Takṣaka, by whom my father was harmed.

sanskrit: ṛṣer hi śṛṅger vacanaṃ kṛtvā dagdhvā ca pārthivam yadi gacched asau pāpo nanu jīvet pitā mama
english: For had that wicked one, after fulfilling the words of the sage Śṛṅgin and burning the king, gone away — surely my father would be alive.

sanskrit: parihīyeta kiṃ tasya yadi jīvet sa pārthivaḥ kāśyapasya prasādena mantriṇāṃ sunayena ca
english: What would have been lost to him if that king had lived, by the grace of Kāśyapa and by the good counsel of the ministers?

sanskrit: sa tu vāritavān mohāt kāśyapaṃ dvijasattamam saṃjijīvayiṣuṃ prāptaṃ rājānam aparājitam
english: But he, out of delusion, turned away Kāśyapa, the best of twice-born ones, who had come to revive the invincible king.

sanskrit: mahān atikramo hy eṣa takṣakasya durātmanaḥ dvijasya yo 'dadad dravyaṃ mā nṛpaṃ jīvayed iti
english: This is a great transgression by the wicked-souled Takṣaka — that he gave wealth to the brahmin so that the king might not be revived.

sanskrit: uttaṅkasya priyaṃ kurvann ātmanaś ca mahat priyam bhavatāṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ yāsyāmy apacitiṃ pituḥ
english: Doing what is dear to Uttaṅka, what is greatly dear to myself, and dear to all of you — I shall take vengeance for my father."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca evam uktvā tataḥ śrīmān mantribhiś cānumoditaḥ āruroha pratijñāṃ sa sarpasatrāya pārthivaḥ brahman bharataśārdūlo rājā pārikṣitas tadā
english: The Sūta said: Having spoken thus, that glorious king, approved by his ministers, O brahmin, then undertook the vow for the snake sacrifice — that tiger of the Bharatas, king Pārikṣita Janamejaya.

sanskrit: purohitam athāhūya ṛtvijaṃ vasudhādhipaḥ abravīd vākyasaṃpannaḥ saṃpadarthakaraṃ vacaḥ
english: Having summoned the household priest and the sacrificial priests, the lord of the earth, gifted in speech, uttered words that were purposeful and apt:

sanskrit: yo me hiṃsitavāṃs tātaṃ takṣakaḥ sa durātmavān pratikuryāṃ yathā tasya tad bhavanto bruvantu me
english: "That evil-minded Takṣaka who harmed my father — how I may retaliate against him: tell me that, gentlemen.

sanskrit: api tat karma viditaṃ bhavatāṃ yena pannagam takṣakaṃ saṃpradīpte 'gnau prāpsye 'haṃ sahabāndhavam
english: Is the method known to you by which I may bring Takṣaka, the serpent, together with his kinsmen, into the blazing fire?

sanskrit: yathā tena pitā mahyaṃ pūrvaṃ dagdho viṣāgninā tathāham api taṃ pāpaṃ dagdhum icchāmi pannagam
english: Just as my father was formerly burned by him with the fire of venom, so too do I wish to burn that wicked serpent."

sanskrit: ṛtvija ūcuḥ asti rājan mahat satraṃ tvadarthaṃ devanirmitam sarpasatram iti khyātaṃ purāṇe kathyate nṛpa
english: The priests said: There exists, O king, a great sacrifice ordained by the gods for your purpose; it is known as the Sarpasatra — the snake sacrifice — and is spoken of in the Purāṇas, O king.

sanskrit: āhartā tasya satrasya tvan nānyo 'sti narādhipa iti paurāṇikāḥ prāhur asmākaṃ cāsti sa kratuḥ
english: "You and no other are the one to perform that sacrifice, O lord of men" — so the Purāṇic authorities declare; and that rite is within our knowledge."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca evam uktaḥ sa rājarṣir mene sarpaṃ hi takṣakam hutāśanamukhaṃ dīptaṃ praviṣṭam iti sattama
english: The Sūta said: Thus addressed, that royal seer imagined the serpent Takṣaka already entered into the blazing mouth of the fire god, O good one.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīn mantravidas tān rājā brāhmaṇāṃs tadā āhariṣyāmi tat satraṃ saṃbhārāḥ saṃbhriyantu me
english: Then the king, knower of sacred formulas, said to those brahmins: "I shall perform that sacrifice — let the materials be assembled for me."

sanskrit: tatas te ṛtvijas tasya śāstrato dvijasattama deśaṃ taṃ māpayām āsur yajñāyatanakāraṇāt yathāvaj jñānaviduṣaḥ sarve buddhyā paraṃ gatāḥ
english: Then those priests of his, O best of twice-born ones, measured out the ground according to scripture for the purpose of establishing the sacrificial site; all of them were knowers of sacred science, their minds reaching the highest wisdom.

sanskrit: ṛddhyā paramayā yuktam iṣṭaṃ dvijagaṇāyutam prabhūtadhanadhānyāḍhyam ṛtvigbhiḥ suniveśitam
english: It was endowed with supreme prosperity, delightful, thronged with multitudes of twice-born ones, abundantly rich in wealth and grain, well laid out by the officiating priests.

sanskrit: nirmāya cāpi vidhivad yajñāyatanam īpsitam rājānaṃ dīkṣayām āsuḥ sarpasatrāptaye tadā
english: Having properly constructed the desired sacrificial ground according to rule, they then initiated the king for the attainment of the snake sacrifice.

sanskrit: idaṃ cāsīt tatra pūrvaṃ sarpasatre bhaviṣyati nimittaṃ mahad utpannaṃ yajñavighnakaraṃ tadā
english: And there had arisen previously at that snake sacrifice a great portent — a sign that an obstacle to the sacrifice would come.

sanskrit: yajñasyāyatane tasmin kriyamāṇe vaco 'bravīt sthapatir buddhisaṃpanno vāstuvidyāviśāradaḥ
english: When the sacrificial ground was being laid out, the master-builder, endowed with intelligence and learned in the science of architecture, spoke these words:

sanskrit: ity abravīt sūtradhāraḥ sūtaḥ paurāṇikas tadā yasmin deśe ca kāle ca māpaneyaṃ pravartitā brāhmaṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ kṛtvā nāyaṃ saṃsthāsyate kratuḥ
english: Thus spoke the master-builder, the versed narrator of Purāṇas at that time: "In the place and at the time when this measuring was initiated, owing to a brahmin being the cause, this sacrifice will not be completed."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu rājā sa prāgdīkṣākālam abravīt kṣattāraṃ neha me kaś cid ajñātaḥ praviśed iti
english: Having heard this, the king said to the doorkeeper before the time of his initiation: "Let no one unknown to me enter here."

sanskrit: tataḥ karma pravavṛte sarpasatre vidhānataḥ paryakrāmaṃś ca vidhivat sve sve karmaṇi yājakāḥ
english: Then the work of the snake sacrifice began according to rule, and the officiating priests went about properly, each in his own assigned duty.

sanskrit: paridhāya kṛṣṇavāsāṃsi dhūmasaṃraktalocanāḥ juhuvur mantravac caiva samiddhaṃ jātavedasam
english: Having put on dark garments, their eyes reddened by smoke, they poured oblations with sacred formulas into the well-kindled fire.

sanskrit: kampayantaś ca sarveṣām uragāṇāṃ manāṃsi te sarpān ājuhuvus tatra sarvān agnimukhe tadā
english: Causing the minds of all serpents to tremble, they summoned all the snakes there into the mouth of fire.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarpāḥ samāpetuḥ pradīpte havyavāhane viveṣṭamānāḥ kṛpaṇā āhvayantaḥ parasparam
english: Then the serpents fell into the blazing sacrificial fire, writhing pitifully, calling out to one another.

sanskrit: visphurantaḥ śvasantaś ca veṣṭayantas tathā pare pucchaiḥ śirobhiś ca bhṛśaṃ citrabhānuṃ prapedire
english: Some wriggling, others hissing, others coiling — they entered the fire of many colours head-first and tail-first repeatedly.

sanskrit: śvetāḥ kṛṣṇāś ca nīlāś ca sthavirāḥ śiśavas tathā ruvanto bhairavān nādān petur dīpte vibhāvasau
english: White ones, black ones, and blue ones — old and young alike — uttering terrible cries, they fell into the blazing fire.

sanskrit: evaṃ śatasahasrāṇi prayutāny arbudāni ca avaśāni vinaṣṭāni pannagānāṃ dvijottama
english: In this way hundreds of thousands, millions, and tens of millions of serpents were helplessly destroyed, O best of twice-born ones.

sanskrit: indurā iva tatrānye hastihastā ivāpare mattā iva ca mātaṅgā mahākāyā mahābalāḥ
english: Some were there like elephants with their trunks, others with limbs like elephant trunks, others like maddened elephants — all of great body and great strength.

sanskrit: uccāvacāś ca bahavo nānāvarṇā viṣolbaṇāḥ ghorāś ca parighaprakhyā dandaśūkā mahābalāḥ prapetur agnāv uragā mātṛvāgdaṇḍapīḍitāḥ
english: Many of various sizes, of diverse colours, teeming with venom, terrible, like iron clubs, great serpents of great strength — all fell into the fire, tormented by the rod of their mother's words.

sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca sarpasatre tadā rājñaḥ pāṇḍaveyasya dhīmataḥ janamejayasya ke tv āsann ṛtvijaḥ paramarṣayaḥ
english: Śaunaka said: At that snake sacrifice of the wise king Janamejaya, descendant of the Pāṇḍavas, who were the officiating priests — the greatest of sages?

sanskrit: ke sadasyā babhūvuś ca sarpasatre sudāruṇe viṣādajanane 'tyarthaṃ pannagānāṃ mahābhaye
english: Who were the attending sages at that dreadful snake sacrifice — so exceedingly producing despair, in that great terror for the serpents?

sanskrit: sarvaṃ vistaratas tāta bhavāñ śaṃsitum arhati sarpasatravidhānajñā vijñeyās te hi sūtaja
english: You ought to relate everything in detail, dear one — for you are known as knowledgeable in the procedure of the snake sacrifice, O son of the Sūta.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca hanta te kathayiṣyāmi nāmānīha manīṣiṇām ye ṛtvijaḥ sadasyāś ca tasyāsan nṛpates tadā
english: The Sūta said: Come, I shall tell you here the names of the wise men who were the officiating priests and attending sages of that king at that time.

sanskrit: tatra hotā babhūvātha brāhmaṇaś caṇḍabhārgavaḥ cyavanasyānvaye jātaḥ khyāto vedavidāṃ varaḥ
english: There the Hotā priest was the brahmin Caṇḍabhārgava, born in the lineage of Cyavana, renowned as the best among knowers of the Veda.

sanskrit: udgātā brāhmaṇo vṛddho vidvān kautsāryajaiminiḥ brahmābhavac chārṅgaravo adhvaryur bodhapiṅgalaḥ
english: The Udgātā was the aged and learned brahmin Kautsāryajaimini; the Brahman priest was Śārṅgarava, and the Adhvaryu was Bodhapiṅgala.

sanskrit: sadasyaś cābhavad vyāsaḥ putraśiṣyasahāyavān uddālakaḥ śamaṭhakaḥ śvetaketuś ca pañcamaḥ
english: Among the attending sages was Vyāsa, accompanied by his sons and disciples; Uddālaka; Śamaṭhaka; and Śvetaketu as the fifth.

sanskrit: asito devalaś caiva nāradaḥ parvatas tathā ātreyaḥ kuṇḍajaṭharo dvijaḥ kuṭighaṭas tathā
english: Asita and Devala; Nārada and Parvata likewise; Ātreya; the twice-born Kuṇḍajaṭhara; and Kuṭighaṭa as well.

sanskrit: vātsyaḥ śrutaśravā vṛddhas tapaḥsvādhyāyaśīlavān kahoḍo devaśarmā ca maudgalyaḥ śamasaubharaḥ
english: Vātsya; the aged Śrutaśravā, devoted to austerity and self-study; Kahoḍa; Devaśarmā; Maudgalya; and Śamasaubhara.
